> Contract: every feature of transaction $e_t$ is computed only from events with step $< \tau_t$ (intra-step permutation invariant); stripped columns are removed at ingestion and asserted absent before featurisation.
> Causal feature vector: 32 features (log-amount, hour, one-hot type, velocity windows [1, 5, 20] steps, per-entity running moments, pre-event ledger balance and deltas). Verified labels are released with a 1–14 day dispute/chargeback delay (one window in the drift protocol).

> Mean ± std over 50 chronological test windows (paysim); best value per column in bold. EML: mean realised asymmetric monetary + friction loss per transaction under each model's own policy (CS-ACRC four-action routing for MG-ECFM, approve/block at the operating threshold for BP1–BP4).
> Latency: amortised batch-scoring time per transaction (ms) on CPU; the single-transaction authorisation path of MG-ECFM is profiled separately in the dashboard / quick demo.
> p (Wilcoxon): Holm-adjusted two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on per-window PR-AUC versus MG-ECFM; (+) MG-ECFM higher, (−) MG-ECFM lower. p (McNemar): Holm-adjusted McNemar test on paired per-transaction correctness at the operating thresholds.

| B5 Assist OFF | ✓ | ✓ | adaptive | ✓ | ✗ | 0.283 | **0.392** | 0.0006 | 441.1 | 414.53M | 57.1 | 0 |

> Pooled over all test windows (paysim). Graph: camouflage-filtered temporal GraphSAGE + DAE residual; Gate: ✓ martingale e-process admission/rollback, auto = every candidate admitted, ✗ = no KB; CRC: static / adaptive CS-ACRC four-action routing or binary approve/block; Rec.: TD-TPF post-incident recovery; Assist: retrieval-based analyst assist (off the decision path).
> Net loss = realised policy loss − recovered value + recovery cost (monetary units). Prevented: share of fraud value intercepted pre-settlement or recovered within the 24 h window. B3 adaptive, B4 and B5 branch from one fitted pipeline, so they share ranking metrics by construction.

### Table 4. Adversarial knowledge-poisoning stress test and Ville's-bound verification of the martingale e-process gate.

| $\rho$ | Realised | FAR gate (%) | FAR SL-only (%) | FAR auto (%) | Rolled back (%) | TTR mean/max | Ville exact | Ville MC [95% CI] | In-gate | Bound |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 5% | 5.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 100.0 | 100.0 | 1.05 / 2 | 0.0365 | 0.0349 [0.031, 0.039] | 0.0211 | ✓ |
| 10% | 10.0 | 0.0 | 2.1 | 100.0 | 100.0 | 1.00 / 1 | 0.0365 | 0.0356 [0.032, 0.039] | 0.0000 | ✓ |
| 15% | 15.0 | 1.6 | 1.6 | 100.0 | 100.0 | 1.13 / 3 | 0.0365 | 0.0351 [0.032, 0.039] | 0.0122 | ✓ |
| 20% | 20.0 | 1.5 | 1.5 | 100.0 | 100.0 | 1.16 / 4 | 0.0365 | 0.0361 [0.033, 0.040] | 0.0000 | ✓ |
| 25% | 25.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 100.0 | 100.0 | 1.12 / 5 | 0.0365 | 0.0404 [0.037, 0.044] | 0.0000 | ✓ |

> FAR: share of harmful (poisoned, Sybil, stale, conflicting) candidates ever admitted to the active KB. Admission test $H_0$: precision $\leq p_0$ = 0.50 at $\alpha_{admit}$ = 0.05; rollback test $H_0^{good}$: FPR $\leq q_0$ = 0.20 at $\alpha_{roll}$ = 0.05.
> Rollback / TTR: harmful rules injected directly into the active KB; share rolled back and mean / max update cycles to rollback (8 verified firings per cycle).
> Ville's inequality $P(\sup_t M_t \geq 1/\alpha) \leq \alpha$ = 0.05 under $H_0$: exact crossing probability over the horizon, Monte-Carlo rate with 95% Clopper-Pearson interval, and the false-rollback rate of genuine rules inside the gate. ✓: bound satisfied by all three checks.
